87: /-- A version of `fundamental_theorem_of_variational_calculus'` for `Continuous f`.
88: The proof uses assumption that source of `f` is finite-dimensional
89: inner-product space, so that a bump function with compact support exists via
90: `ContDiffBump.hasCompactSupport` from `Analysis.Calculus.BumpFunction.Basic`.
91: 
92: The proof is by contradiction, assume that there is `x₀` such that `f x₀ ≠ 0` then one construct
93: construct `g` test function *supported* on the neighborhood of `x₀` such that `⟪f x, g x⟫ ≥ 0`
94: and `⟪f x, g x⟫ > 0` on a neighborhood of x₀.
95: 
96: Using `Y` for the theorem below to make use of bump functions in InnerProductSpaces. `Y` is
97: a finite dimensional measurable space over `ℝ` with (standard) inner product.
98: -/
99: lemma fundamental_theorem_of_variational_calculus' {f : Y → V}
100:     (μ : Measure Y) [IsFiniteMeasureOnCompacts μ] [μ.IsOpenPosMeasure]
101:     [OpensMeasurableSpace Y]
102:     (hf : Continuous f) (hg : ∀ g, IsTestFunction g → ∫ x, ⟪f x, g x⟫_ℝ ∂μ = 0) :
103:     f = 0 := by
104:   -- assume ¬(f = 0)
105:     rw [funext_iff]; by_contra h₀
106:     obtain ⟨x₀, hx0⟩ := not_forall.1 h₀
107:     simp at hx0 -- hx0 : f x₀ ≠ 0
108: 
109:   -- [1] Proof that `f` is continuous at `x₀`.
110:   -- Embed into the true IP-space `WithLp 2 V`.
111:     let f₂ : Y → WithLp 2 V := toL2 ℝ ∘ f
112:     let x₂ := f₂ x₀
113:   -- x₂ ≠ 0 because `fromL2 (toL2 (f x₀)) = f x₀`
114:     have hx2 : x₂ ≠ 0 := by
115:       intro h; apply hx0; exact congrArg (fromL2 ℝ) h
116:   -- continuity of f₂ at x₀
117:     have hcont₂ : ContinuousAt f₂ x₀ := ((toL2 ℝ).continuous.comp hf).continuousAt
118: 
119:   -- [2] find open neighborhood guaranteeing positive inner product with the center, based on
120:   -- which the test function `g` will be constructed.
121:   -- pick δ₂ so that on B(x₀, δ₂), ‖f₂ x - x₂‖ < ‖x₂‖/2
122:     obtain ⟨δ₂, hδ₂_pos, hδ₂⟩ :=
123:     Metric.continuousAt_iff.mp hcont₂ (‖x₂‖ / 2)
124:       (by simpa [half_pos] using (norm_pos_iff.mpr hx2))
125:   -- now the usual “add & subtract” proof inside WithLp 2 V
126:     have inner_pos₂ : ∀ x (hx : x ∈ Metric.ball x₀ δ₂), 0 < (⟪f₂ x, x₂⟫_ℝ : ℝ) := by
127:       intros x hx
128:     -- hx : x ∈ ball x₀ δ₂, so dist x x₀ < δ₂, hence
129:     -- this is |⟪u,v⟫| ≤ ‖u‖ * ‖v‖, in the genuine InnerProductSpace on WithLp 2 V
130:       have hclose : ‖f₂ x - x₂‖ < ‖x₂‖ / 2 := by
131:         convert hδ₂ hx using 1
132:         exact mem_sphere_iff_norm.mp rfl
133:       have hself : ⟪x₂, x₂⟫_ℝ = ‖x₂‖^2 := real_inner_self_eq_norm_sq (x₂ : WithLp 2 V)
134:       -- Cauchy–Schwarz in `WithLp 2 V` bounds the cross term from below
135:       have hcs : -(‖f₂ x - x₂‖ * ‖x₂‖) ≤ ⟪f₂ x - x₂, x₂⟫_ℝ :=
136:         neg_le_of_abs_le (abs_real_inner_le_norm _ _)
137:       have hxp : 0 < ‖x₂‖ := norm_pos_iff.mpr hx2
138:       have inner_eq_self_add_diff : ⟪f₂ x, x₂⟫_ℝ = ⟪x₂, x₂⟫_ℝ + ⟪f₂ x - x₂, x₂⟫_ℝ := by
139:         rw [← inner_add_left]; simp
140:       nlinarith [inner_eq_self_add_diff, hcs, hself, hclose, hxp,
141:         mul_lt_mul_of_pos_right hclose hxp]
142:   -- pull `inner_pos₂` back to V via `fromL2`:
143:     have inner_pos_V : ∀ x ∈ Metric.ball x₀ δ₂, 0 < ⟪f x, f x₀⟫_ℝ := fun x hx => inner_pos₂ x hx
144:     -- now we have a genuine positive integrand on a set of positive measure.
145: 
146:   -- [3] `g` construction using bump function.
147:     have bump_exists : ∃ φ : Y → ℝ, IsTestFunction φ ∧ φ x₀ > 0 ∧
148:         (∀ x ∈ Function.support φ, 0 ≤ φ x) ∧
149:         Function.support φ ⊆ Metric.ball x₀ (δ₂/2) ∧
150:         (∀ x ∈ Metric.closedBall x₀ (δ₂/4), 0 < φ x) := by
151:         -- use `hasContDiffBump_of_innerProductSpace`, leveraging `[innerProductSpace Y]`
152:           haveI : HasContDiffBump Y := hasContDiffBump_of_innerProductSpace Y
153:           let φ1 : ContDiffBump x₀ :=
154:             ⟨δ₂ / 4, δ₂ / 2, by positivity, by linarith⟩
155:           refine ⟨φ1.toFun, ⟨φ1.contDiff, φ1.hasCompactSupport⟩,
156:             φ1.pos_of_mem_ball (Metric.mem_ball_self φ1.rOut_pos), fun x _ => φ1.nonneg,
157:             by rw [ContDiffBump.support_eq], fun x hx => φ1.pos_of_mem_ball ?_⟩
158:         -- the closed ball of radius `δ₂/4` lies in the open ball of radius `rOut = δ₂/2`
159:           rw [Metric.mem_closedBall] at hx
160:           exact Metric.mem_ball.mpr (lt_of_le_of_lt hx (by show δ₂ / 4 < δ₂ / 2; linarith))
161:     obtain ⟨φ, hφ_testfun, hφ_pos_x₀, hφ_non_neg, hφ_support_subset, hφ_pos_inner⟩ :=
162:       bump_exists
163:   -- Define test function g(x) = φ(x) * f(x₀)
164:     let g : Y → V := fun x => φ x • f x₀
165:   -- Show that g is a test function: `φ` is a test function and `f x₀` is smooth (constant)
166:     have hg_test : IsTestFunction g := IsTestFunction.smul_right hφ_testfun contDiff_const
167: 
168:   -- [4] Derive contradiction. First compute the integral ∫ ⟪f x, g x⟫
169:   -- [4.1] ∫ φ x * ⟪f x, f x₀⟫ = 0
170:     have key_integral := hg g hg_test
171:   -- linearity of inner product in the second argument turns the integrand into `φ x * ⟪f x, f x₀⟫`
172:     simp only [g, inner_smul_right'] at key_integral
173: 
174:   -- [4.2] 0 < ∫ x, φ x * ⟪f x, f x₀⟫_ℝ ∂μ. Sketch: on the support of φ (which is contained in
175:   -- B(x₀, δ/2) ⊆ B(x₀, δ)), we have ⟪f x, f x₀⟫ > ‖f x₀‖²/2 > 0 by our choice of δ.
176:   -- Since φ is nonnegative on its support and positive somewhere, this gives the contradiction.
177: 
178:   -- [4.2.1] Integrability of the integrand: `integrable_prod` .
179:     have support_subset : Function.support φ ⊆ Metric.ball x₀ δ₂ :=
180:       hφ_support_subset.trans (Metric.ball_subset_ball (by linarith))
181:     have supp_subset2 : Function.support (fun x => φ x * ⟪f x, f x₀⟫_ℝ) ⊆ Function.support φ := by
182:       intro x hprod hφ0
183:     -- if φ x = 0 then φ x * inner = 0, contradiction
184:       simp [hφ0] at hprod
185:     have hinner_cont : Continuous (fun x => ⟪f x, f x₀⟫_ℝ) :=
186:       Continuous.inner' (f : Y → V) (fun _ => f x₀) hf continuous_const
187:     have integrable_prod :
188:       Integrable (fun x => φ x * ⟪f x, f x₀⟫_ℝ) μ :=
189:     -- (i) build a `HasCompactSupport` witness for the product
190:       (Continuous.mul hφ_testfun.smooth.continuous hinner_cont).integrable_of_hasCompactSupport
191:         (hφ_testfun.supp.mono supp_subset2)
192: 
193:   -- [4.2.2] Nonnegativity everywhere (`h_nonneg`)
194:     have h_nonneg : ∀ x, 0 ≤ φ x * ⟪f x, f x₀⟫_ℝ := by
195:       intro x
196:       by_cases hx : x ∈ Function.support φ
197:       · -- on the support, φ ≥ 0 and ⟪f x, f x₀⟫ > 0
198:         exact mul_nonneg (hφ_non_neg x hx) (inner_pos_V x (support_subset hx)).le
199:       · -- off the support, φ x = 0 so the product is 0
200:         simp [Function.notMem_support.mp hx]
201: 
202:   -- [4.2.3] That closed ball has positive measure, and is contained in the support
203:     -- every nonempty open set has positive measure
204:     have hμ_ball : 0 < μ (Metric.ball x₀ (δ₂/4)) :=
205:       Metric.isOpen_ball.measure_pos μ (Metric.nonempty_ball.mpr (by linarith))
206:     have hμ : 0 < μ (Metric.closedBall x₀ (δ₂/4)) :=
207:       lt_of_lt_of_le hμ_ball (measure_mono Metric.ball_subset_closedBall)
208:     have closedBall_subset_support :
209:         Metric.closedBall x₀ (δ₂/4)
210:           ⊆ Function.support (fun x => φ x * ⟪f x, f x₀⟫_ℝ) := by
211:         intro x hx
212:         have hφx := hφ_pos_inner x hx
213:         have hin : 0 < ⟪f x, f x₀⟫_ℝ :=
214:           inner_pos_V x (Metric.closedBall_subset_ball (by linarith) hx)
215:         simp only [Function.support_mul, Set.mem_inter_iff, Function.mem_support, ne_eq]
216:         constructor
217:         · linarith
218:         · linarith
219: 
220:   -- [4.2.4] putting everything together: positivity contradicts `key_integral : ∫ ... = 0`
221:     have integral_pos : 0 < ∫ x, φ x * ⟪f x, f x₀⟫_ℝ ∂μ :=
222:       (integral_pos_iff_support_of_nonneg h_nonneg integrable_prod).mpr
223:         (lt_of_lt_of_le hμ (measure_mono closedBall_subset_support))
224:     linarith

233:     [OpensMeasurableSpace X]
234:     (hf : IsTestFunction f) (hg : ∀ g, IsTestFunction g → ∫ x, ⟪f x, g x⟫_ℝ ∂μ = 0) :
235:     f = 0 := by
236:   have hf' := hg f hf
237:   rw [MeasureTheory.integral_eq_zero_iff_of_nonneg] at hf'
238:   · rw [Continuous.ae_eq_iff_eq] at hf'

240:       have hf'' := congrFun hf' x

244:     · fun_prop
245:   · intro x
246:     simp only [Pi.zero_apply]
